A weight of magnitude $40\text{ kg.wt}$ is suspended from $A$ and the rod begins to rotate about $C$. Find the distance from the point of action of the rod weight to $A$, then find the maximum weight that can be suspended from $B$ and lifting the suspended weight from $A$ without getting imbalanced.
options: distance $20\text{ cm}$, maximum weight $= 50\text{ kg wt}$
distance $30\text{ cm}$, maximum weight $= 80\text{ kg wt}$

questions.q: A uniform rod $AB$ of length $260\text{ cm}$ and weight $43\text{ N}$ rests on a vertical wall with its end $A$, and on a rough horizontal ground with its end $B$. If the two coefficients of friction between the rod and both the wall and ground are equal to $1/4$ and $1/2$ respectively. If the end $B$ is at distant $100\text{ cm}$ from the wall, find the horizontal force acting at the end $B$ to make the rod be about to move towards the wall.
A particle moves with a constant speed of $25\text{ m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ in a $90\text{ m}$ radius circle. how many revolutions does it make in $30\text{ s}$?
A cyclist accelerates constantly from rest. After $8\text{ s}$, the wheels have rotated $3\text{ rev}$. What is the angular speed of the wheels at the end of the $8\text{ s}$?

A car has wheels of radius $30\text{ cm}$. It starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to a speed of $15\text{ m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ in a time of $8.0\text{ s}$. Find the angular acceleration of its wheels.

A string wound on the rim of a wheel $20\text{ cm}$ in diameter is pulled out at a rate of $75\text{ cm}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$. Through how many revolutions will the wheel have turned by the time that $9.0\text{ m}$ of string has been unwound? How long will it take?
A wheel of mass $6.0\text{ kg}$ and radius of gyration $40\text{ cm}$ is rotating at $300\text{ rpm}$. Find its moment of inertia and its rotational $KE$.
An airplane propeller has a mass of $70\text{ kg}$ and a radius of gyration of $75\text{ cm}$. How large a torque is needed to give it an angular acceleration of $4.0\text{ rev}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$?

As shown in the following figure, a uniform solid sphere rolls on a horizontal surface at $20\text{ m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ and then rolls up the incline. If friction losses are negligible, what will be the value of $h$ where the ball stops? (Hint: $I_{\text{sphere}}=\frac{2}{5}mr^{2}$)

A flywheel has a moment of inertia of $3.8\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^{2}$. What constant torque is required to increase its frequency from $2.0\text{ rev}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ to $5.0\text{ rev}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ in $6.0$ revolutions?

To get some exercise without going anywhere, you set your bike on a stand so that the rear wheel is free to turn. As you pedal, the chain applies a force of $18\text{ N}$ to the rear sprocket wheel at a distance of $r_{s}=7.0\text{ cm}$ from the rotation axis of the wheel. Consider the wheel to be a hoop ($I=MR^{2}$) of radius $R=35\text{ cm}$ and mass $M=2.4\text{ kg}$. What is the angular velocity of the wheel after $5.0\text{ s}$?

As shown in the following figure, a mass $m=400\text{ g}$ hangs from the rim of a wheel of radius $r=15\text{ cm}$. When released from rest, the mass falls $2.0\text{ m}$ in $6.5\text{ s}$. Find the moment of inertia of the wheel.

An ice skater begins a spin by rotating at an angular velocity of $2\text{ rad}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ with both arms and one leg outstretched. At that time her moment of inertia is $0.5\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^{2}$. She then brings her arms up over her head and her legs together, reducing her moment of inertia by $0.2\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^{2}$. At what angular velocity will she then spin?
